title: Nothing from Something: Can a Language Model Discover 0?
analysis: Spontaneously producing zero on held-out tasks and learning it from a few examples are different tests. The authors report improvement in sample efficiency from language pretraining, while the zero-shot result remained negative at the tested model scale.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: MemTrace: Probing What Final Accuracy Misses in Long-Term Memory
analysis: Several questions can refer to one underlying fact. Evaluate whether the agent can retrieve its older value, explain a change and reject a false premise. In these experiments reachable evidence often went unused, so expanding storage alone would miss the reported bottleneck.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: SkillChain-Gym: A Benchmark for Reskilling-Aware Production-Inventory Control under Disruptions
analysis: Training consumes hours that could make inventory today while protecting against future certification gaps. Compare adaptive and fixed training schedules under both forecasted and surprise shortages; a policy ranking from one regime does not transfer automatically.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: SproutRAG: Attention-Guided Tree Search with Progressive Embeddings for Long-Document RAG
analysis: Building a sentence tree lets the retriever return a small factual span or a larger coherent passage. The reported gain is in information efficiency. Compare downstream answer fidelity at equal retrieved-token budgets before translating it into a quality or cost claim.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Gaussian Mixture Attention: Linear-Time Sequence Mixing via Probabilistic Latent Routing
analysis: Routing through a fixed number of latent components replaces a dense pairwise activation with two token-by-component matrices. Fixed-component memory scaling says little about throughput at a given sequence length; the authors report optimized causal baselines still ahead in their implementation.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Pointwise is Pointless? A Multimodal Ablation Study for Precipitation Nowcasting with Graph Neural Networks
analysis: A forecast can improve rain onset at individual stations without improving the spatial radar field. Score the two targets separately and include early false rain alerts when choosing between deterministic and probabilistic variants.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Continuous Audio Thinking for Large Audio Language Models
analysis: The proposed workspace preserves acoustic features before text generation. It avoids additional autoregressive decoding steps; prefill computation, expert supervision and end-to-end latency are separate costs to measure.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: CoreMem: Riemannian Retrieval and Fisher-Guided Distillation for Long-Term Memory in Dialogue Agents
analysis: Adaptive retrieval and compression are distinct contributors to a personalized memory system. The reported temporal gains and 8 GB VRAM budget apply to the tested edge-cloud architecture. They do not establish that the entire pipeline works offline on every 8 GB machine.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: MLLP-VRAIN UPV system for the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task
analysis: Context can help at two different stages: recognition of domain words and selection of translated examples. The reported English-to-German improvement concerns a particular test set; compare latency and quality per direction before carrying it over to other languages.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Speaking in Self-Assessing Tongues: On the Verbalized Confidence of LLMs in Machine Translation
analysis: Similar aggregate calibration scores can hide disagreement about which individual words are wrong. If using verbal confidence to trigger human review, measure errors caught at a fixed review budget for the actual model and language pair.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Not Truly Multilingual: Script Consistency as a Missing Dimension in VLM Evaluation
analysis: Holding image and question meaning fixed while varying Punjabi script isolates a failure that aggregate language accuracy hides. Check consistency across scripts for the same item. An improvement from adding an image can coexist with a persistent script gap.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Redact or Keep? A Fully Local AI Cascade for Educational Dialogue De-Identification
analysis: The first stage proposes possible identifiers broadly. A second stage uses speaker role and context to distinguish a student name from a curricular term. Audit missed candidates separately: the reviewer cannot redact a span it never receives. The reported 0.958 macro F1 is a two-platform benchmark result, not a guarantee of de-identification.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: CODEBLOCK: Learning to Supervise Code at the Right Granularity
analysis: The training procedure keeps the whole response as context while applying loss to selected syntactic blocks. A smaller fraction of supervised tokens is therefore not an equivalent reduction in input length or total compute. Compare parser-aligned blocks with isolated tokens at the same loss budget.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Quantifying Consistency in LLM Logical Reasoning via Structural Uncertainty
analysis: The paper distinguishes unstable judgments across repeats from several equally plausible paths within one trial. Their associations with correctness differ, so summing them as one uncertainty score can obscure failure. The authors find a boundary on factual retrieval tasks.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Searching for Synergy in Shared Workspace Human-AI Collaboration
analysis: The comparison studies simulated teams. Shared memory plus explicit gates helped the tested three-person configuration; it does not establish how real human approvers behave or isolate which of the two interventions accounts for the gain.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: JetSpec: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding with Parallel Tree Drafting
analysis: A larger draft tree helps only when verification accepts enough of its prefix to repay the drafting overhead. The reported peak speedups differ on math and open-ended chat; compare end-to-end latency on the intended hardware, workload and concurrency.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Continuous Edge Inference for Traffic Sign Recognition on Embedded Vehicular Hardware
analysis: Scoring individual images misses unstable predictions across consecutive frames and queueing when many signs need classification. The authors report a long streaming run, but average FPS alone cannot certify deadlines or safety across driving conditions.
coverage: Interpretation of the authors’ versioned abstract. Full paper and experimental runs not reviewed.
